title: Validate project scope end to end and document rollout
description: Exercise project and All projects behavior across built-in threads and project-aware plugins, then document compatibility and rollout policy.
design: Use representative multi-project data, direct workspaces and worktrees, plugin deep links, compact UI, reloads, realtime events, and deleted projects. Keep legacy compatibility bounded and explicit.
acceptance_criteria: Automated coverage verifies route, sidebar, plugin SDK, Tasks, and OpenSpec scope behavior; manual QA covers switching and multi-tab use; docs identify legacy routes, Personal behavior, performance limits, and the eventual compatibility cleanup.

title: Scope the built-in thread sidebar and All projects view
description: Show only the selected project's threads in project scope and preserve an aggregate thread view with project identity and filters in All projects.
design: Reuse the existing project-grouped sidebar bootstrap data initially. Keep targeted server queries as the scaling path and preserve thread hierarchy, pinned state, sections, search, unread state, drag and drop, and compact behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Project scope never leaks unrelated threads; All projects shows cross-project threads with clear ownership and project filtering; creation inherits a concrete scope or asks for a project; sidebar behavior and realtime updates have focused tests.

title: Expose application scope to plugin panels
description: Let project-aware plugin app surfaces read the current AppScope and navigate while preserving or deliberately changing it.
design: Ship the new public plugin member with an experimental_ prefix, add it to docs/api_to_audit.md, and update the real and testing plugin hosts. Prefer an additive contract so existing plugins remain compatible.
acceptance_criteria: A plugin panel can distinguish All projects from a concrete project, reacts to switcher changes, preserves scope in its internal navigation, and is covered by plugin SDK contract, app harness, and compatibility tests.

title: Add the global project scope switcher
description: Add an app-shell switcher for selecting a concrete bb Project or the explicit All projects scope.
design: Treat All projects as a view option rather than a project row. Preserve the current surface where possible and keep per-scope view state without using local state as the source of truth.
acceptance_criteria: The switcher is available on scoped desktop and compact layouts, reflects the route, changes scope without losing deterministic navigation, and handles deleted or unavailable projects safely.

title: Define the AppScope domain and route contract
description: Define the explicit all-projects versus concrete-project scope used by the app shell and project-aware plugin surfaces.
design: Use a discriminated union rather than nullable projectId. Specify Personal and routes outside project scope deliberately. Parse at route boundaries and pass typed scope internally.
acceptance_criteria: The contract distinguishes all-projects, a concrete project, and non-scoped routes without ambiguity; route helpers and focused tests cover every case; docs/project-scope.md matches the implemented semantics.

title: Implement scope-aware routes and navigation compatibility
description: Encode application scope in refreshable URLs and make navigation preserve it across compose, thread, and plugin surfaces.
design: Add canonical scoped routes additively and retain redirects or compatibility handling for existing thread and plugin URLs. Keep browser history and independent tabs deterministic.
acceptance_criteria: Concrete-project and All projects links survive refresh, back and forward navigation, and multiple tabs; existing supported deep links continue to resolve; route history tests cover scope transitions.

title: Make Project the primary bb application scope
description: Make a concrete bb Project the normal application context while preserving an explicit All projects mode for cross-project threads, plugin surfaces, search, and filters.
design: Introduce one explicit AppScope union shared by routing and plugin presentation. Project remains the ownership boundary; Environment remains the concrete workspace for a thread. All projects is a view scope, never a synthetic project.
acceptance_criteria: Users can switch between a concrete project and All projects; threads and project-aware plugin surfaces follow that scope; deep links and refresh preserve it; project-owned mutations always resolve one concrete project; the behavior is available through supported app, SDK, and CLI surfaces where applicable.
notes: Architecture proposal: docs/project-scope.md. Discussion thread: thr_rzvjq7saqx.

title: Exercise offline handoff end to end and document operations
description: Validate the complete Jira-to-central-to-personal-bb lifecycle under realistic network loss, restarts, duplicate events, concurrent claims, Git conflicts, authorization changes, and reconnect publication, then document deployment and support procedures.
design: Use real databases and representative repositories rather than mocked persistence. Include a network cut after package download, personal-bb restart while offline, central restart during reconnaissance, and an audit review of the published result.
acceptance_criteria: Automated integration coverage proves offline continuation and safe reconnect behavior; a manual QA runbook covers setup and recovery; architecture, security, CLI, SDK, plugin, Jira, and operator documentation are discoverable and current.

title: Publish offline results on reconnect and update Jira
description: Allow a locally owned offline task to publish a deliberate result after reconnect: Git branch or commit and optional PR, structured summary, validation evidence, status, and follow-up needs.
design: Publication is explicit rather than background conversation replication. Use the original package and claim versions for conflict detection, make retries idempotent, preserve local work on rejection, and map accepted outcomes to configurable Jira comments, links, and transitions.
acceptance_criteria: A completed local task can publish once despite retries, Jira receives an attributable summary and code link, superseded or reassigned work cannot silently overwrite newer state, and failed publication remains retryable without losing the local thread or files.

title: Materialize a claimed package into a local Git workspace and thread
description: Turn a downloaded package into a locally owned bb project environment and fresh provider thread, with the required repository revision, continuation context, skills, evidence, and acceptance criteria available before the first agent turn.
design: Clone or reuse an authorized local source, verify the expected remote and base commit, create an isolated branch or worktree, and persist a secret-free agent-only context seed plus visible kickoff prompt. Do not pretend to fork the central provider session.
acceptance_criteria: After materialization the network can be disabled and the employee can inspect and continue the thread, restart personal bb, edit and test the local workspace, and retain package provenance. Dirty repositories, missing commits, and remote mismatches fail safely.

title: Build the personal-bb handoff client and secure enrollment
description: Add a local personal-bb integration that authenticates to the corporate handoff gateway, lists authorized continuation choices, claims one, downloads its immutable package, and stores enough local provenance for later publication.
design: Keep personal bb independent from the central bb database. Store credentials through the supported secret boundary, never log token values, cache package bytes and metadata locally for offline use, and make download and claim retries idempotent.
acceptance_criteria: An employee can enroll, list and claim authorized work from personal bb, restart or disconnect after download without losing the package, and revoke the local client without affecting unrelated local bb data.

title: Orchestrate cross-project repository reconnaissance
description: Run central reconnaissance against the application catalog and selected bb projects, collecting repository evidence and producing one or more bounded continuation choices for the Jira request.
design: A dispatcher owns cross-project thread IDs explicitly because normal bb child hierarchies and workflow agents are project-scoped. Use isolated server worktrees, bounded concurrency and budgets, deterministic result schemas, and evidence citations to repository paths and commits.
acceptance_criteria: One Jira request can inspect multiple authorized repositories and agent profiles, failures remain isolated per candidate, choices include rationale and evidence, and every choice resolves to a concrete repository, base revision, skills, acceptance criteria, and continuation prompt.

title: Expose central offline-handoff SDK, HTTP, and bb CLI surfaces
description: Provide first-class programmatic surfaces for intake status, choices, claim, package download, cancellation, result publication, and audit-safe inspection so local agents and operators do not depend on UI-only behavior.
design: Validate all boundary payloads, use stable typed contracts and explicit pagination, and route host-local operations through the daemon only where required. Update CLI guide and skills with every command and configuration knob.
acceptance_criteria: The supported lifecycle can be driven end to end through both SDK and bb CLI, HTTP schemas are versioned and documented, large artifacts use bounded attachment or download paths, and errors are actionable and machine-readable.

title: Persist dispatch runs, continuation choices, claims, and package revisions
description: Persist the central control-plane state for Jira requests, reconnaissance runs, continuation choices, immutable work-package revisions, employee claims, expiration, cancellation, and result publication.
design: Validate at storage boundaries and keep explicit lifecycle fields. Use compare-and-swap transitions for claim and publish operations, stable idempotency keys for retries, targeted indexed queries, and retained provenance from every package to Jira and source reconnaissance threads.
acceptance_criteria: Concurrent claims settle deterministically, repeated requests are idempotent, restart does not lose active discovery or published state, expired and superseded packages are distinguishable, and lifecycle history is queryable.

title: Ingest Jira work requests into central dispatch
description: Accept Jira issue events and explicit rerun requests as central discovery jobs, preserving Jira identity, version, reporter context, links, and bounded attachment metadata without treating untrusted issue content as instructions.
design: Implement an idempotent webhook or connector boundary with signature verification, replay protection, field normalization, and configurable trigger rules. Store only the references and content needed for routing and reconnaissance.
acceptance_criteria: Creating or updating an eligible Jira issue creates exactly one corresponding dispatch revision, duplicate deliveries are harmless, unsupported or unauthorized issues are rejected safely, and operators can inspect intake failures.

title: Enforce employee identity, authorization, and audit boundaries
description: Add the corporate identity and authorization boundary required for employees to list, claim, download, and publish work packages without exposing the central bb public API or unrelated projects, threads, repositories, or secrets.
design: Put an authenticated gateway or narrowly scoped plugin API in front of the workflow. Authorize every operation against employee identity, Jira visibility, application ownership, and repository policy. Use short-lived claim and download credentials and append-only audit events.
acceptance_criteria: Direct unauthenticated access is not required; users can access only authorized packages and repositories; revocation takes effect; secrets never enter work packages; security-sensitive actions are auditable by actor and request.

title: Define the business-application catalog and routing metadata
description: Define how the central dispatcher maps Jira projects, components, labels, and issue content to business applications, bb projects, Git repositories, owners, skills, agent profiles, and dependency relationships.
design: Use a validated, reviewable catalog representation with stable application and repository identifiers. Keep credentials out of catalog data. Support targeted lookup rather than loading and filtering every catalog row, and define CLI or SDK discovery surfaces alongside any user-facing configuration.
acceptance_criteria: Operators can validate and query the catalog; routing can resolve a Jira request to authorized candidate repositories and agent capabilities; stale or ambiguous mappings produce actionable diagnostics.

title: Specify the offline handoff architecture and lifecycle contract
description: Define the end-to-end boundary between Jira, the central dispatcher, repository reconnaissance, claimable work packages, personal bb, Git, and result publication. Specify which system owns each state and explicitly exclude cross-host or cross-server provider-session migration.
design: Define a versioned work-package schema and lifecycle covering requested, discovering, choices_ready, claimed, materialized_local, result_ready, published, canceled, expired, and superseded. Include idempotency keys, optimistic versions, provenance, compatibility rules, retry semantics, privacy controls, and offline behavior.
acceptance_criteria: The decision document contains sequence diagrams, state transitions, schemas, ownership boundaries, failure recovery, compatibility policy, and a threat-model summary sufficient for independent server and local-client implementation.

title: Jira-to-local offline agent handoff
description: Enable a Jira-originated work request to be investigated by a central bb deployment, routed across business-application repositories and agent capabilities, then claimed into an employee personal bb as a locally owned thread that remains usable offline.
design: The central deployment is a discovery and dispatch control plane, not the owner of employee execution. It emits a versioned, secret-free work package containing repository provenance, evidence, acceptance criteria, skills, and a continuation prompt. A local bb client claims and materializes that package into a fresh local thread and Git workspace; later result publication is explicit and reconnect-safe.
acceptance_criteria: A Jira issue can trigger central reconnaissance, present authorized continuation choices, and produce a claimable work package. An employee can import one choice into personal bb, disconnect from the network, continue the locally persisted thread and workspace, then reconnect and publish a conflict-safe result back to central state and Jira. CLI, SDK, UI, security, audit, and operator documentation are included.

title: Handle conductor disconnect, restart, archive, and deletion safely
description: Implement fail-closed settlement and cleanup for daemon disconnects, process exits, server restart, archive, and confirmed deletion.
design: V1 never silently relaunches a flow after daemon loss. Active runs and tasks settle interrupted with a precise reason; future resume remains gated on a durable ai-conductor attach contract.
acceptance_criteria: Daemon loss cannot duplicate a run, all running projected state reaches a terminal status, archive and deletion cascade through existing hierarchy rules, and reconnect cleanup is covered by integration tests.

title: Exercise native conductor runs end to end
description: Add end-to-end coverage using a deterministic ai-conductor mock flow for manager projection, multiple child sessions, tools, input, interactions, stop, and daemon loss.
design: Test real contracts and migrated in-memory databases; do not mock the database. Use Turbo for package orchestration and capture slow test output to a file.
acceptance_criteria: The full launch-to-settlement path passes in CI, malformed and replayed events are covered, and manual QA instructions verify the native hierarchy and timeline in the app.

title: Ship conductor SDK, HTTP, and bb CLI surfaces
description: Expose start, get, list, input, interrupt, and close through the public SDK, server API, and bb conductor CLI commands.
design: The start contract accepts target and args matching the stable ai-conductor flow launch contract and returns both run and manager thread ids.
acceptance_criteria: Every end-user operation is available through SDK and CLI, command output supports JSON, remote-host path semantics are explicit, and guide templates plus the bundled bb-cli skill are regenerated and tested.

title: Route child thread input and pending interactions to conductor
description: Dispatch send, steer, stop, approvals, and user-question answers from projected child threads through the conductor control channel instead of agent-runtime.
design: Reuse bb pending interaction policy and UI while preserving the conductor task and request identity required for the response.
acceptance_criteria: Child composers support queued input and steering, stop targets the correct session, approvals and questions round-trip once, and stale or rejected controls surface actionable native errors.

title: Expose native conductor run service and manager thread
description: Implement the server service that creates a durable conductor run and its root manager thread, dispatches the host start command, and projects flow-level status, annotations, errors, and final result.
design: The manager is a display-only orchestration root, not an agent-runtime provider session. The launch request is shown as the user input and flow output is native timeline state.
acceptance_criteria: Starting a run returns runId and managerThreadId, the manager lifecycle follows the conductor process, stop settles it once, and no provider session is launched for it.

title: Project conductor sessions into child bb threads
description: Create one child bb thread for every interactive conductor session and route short-lived agent turns, tools, model calls, logs, results, and annotations into the nearest owning timeline.
design: Only user-openable interactive sessions become threads. Nested sessions use bb hierarchy up to the depth cap; deeper nodes flatten while retaining conductor ancestry metadata.
acceptance_criteria: Repeated snapshots create exactly one child per session, native timeline rows update correctly, provider and interaction ids are collision-safe, and manager notifications contain session results without internal-task duplication.

title: Run ai-conductor processes in the host daemon
description: Discover and launch the host-local ai-conductor CLI in the selected environment workspace and bridge its versioned event and control streams.
design: The daemon owns process lifecycle and raw validated transport only. It must not create bb threads or decide projection policy.
acceptance_criteria: Start, input, answer, interrupt, and close work through daemon commands; malformed output is isolated; stderr and exit state are reported; tests cover process races and cleanup.

title: Persist conductor runs and task projection state
description: Add server-owned persistence for conductor runs and the mapping from conductor task ids to manager, owner, and projected child thread ids.
design: Use generated Drizzle migrations. Ingestion must be idempotent by run id and event sequence; resolved profile data must be sanitized before persistence.
acceptance_criteria: Runs and task mappings survive server restart, duplicate events do not duplicate threads or timeline rows, and database tests use migrated in-memory SQLite.

title: Formalize the ai-conductor host JSONL protocol
description: Promote the current private JSONL snapshot and stdin control channel in qwen-workflow into a versioned host integration protocol consumable by bb.
design: Add exported runtime schemas, protocol and capability versions, monotonic event sequence, sanitized profile snapshot, handshake, and acknowledgements for input, answer, interrupt, and close.
acceptance_criteria: A host can detect protocol compatibility before launch, validate every envelope, deduplicate replayed events by sequence, persist a secret-free profile snapshot, and observe control command success or failure.

Discussion thread: thr_4iue3af3bu in qwen-workflow. Initial scope is read-only protocol discussion; implementation is not authorized yet.

title: Add bb conductor domain and host-daemon contracts
description: Define conductor run, task, snapshot, event, lifecycle, command, and response schemas across domain, server-contract, and host-daemon-contract.
design: Keep conductor contracts separate from provider contracts. Fill server-owned defaults at the boundary and pass explicit values over the wire.
acceptance_criteria: All new host commands and daemon messages parse at both boundaries, contract tests cover invalid envelopes, and HOST_DAEMON_PROTOCOL_VERSION is incremented.
notes: Discussion thread: thr_hjenvbuzvx in bb. Initial scope is read-only contract discussion; implementation is not authorized yet.

title: Native ai-conductor runs in bb
description: Implement the native ai-conductor run surface described in docs/ai-conductor-integration.md: a manager bb thread per conductor run, interactive conductor sessions as child threads, and short-lived tasks as native timeline events.
design: ai-conductor is a separate orchestration runtime, not an agent provider. The server owns persistence and projection policy; the host daemon owns the host-local conductor process and validated transport.
acceptance_criteria: A conductor flow can be launched through SDK and bb CLI, observed through a manager thread and child session threads, controlled interactively, and settled safely across stop or daemon loss.

title: Adapt the OpenSpec plugin to consume AppScope
description: Make the owned OpenSpec surface show specifications for one selected project or an aggregate catalog across projects.
design: Project scope resolves the project's available default source; All projects aggregates per-project indexes and retains project identity. Editing resolves a concrete project and source or environment. Handle disconnected hosts as partial availability.
acceptance_criteria: Project scope shows only its specifications; All projects supports project filtering and partial results; every result exposes ownership; create and edit cannot proceed without a concrete project and workspace target.

title: Adapt the Tasks plugin to consume AppScope
description: Make the owned Tasks plugin show tasks for the selected bb Project or all tasks without changing the core bb Tasks data model.
design: In project scope resolve Tasks projects through linked_bb_project_id; in All projects keep the aggregate list and expose project filters. Do not migrate or remove the plugin's own projects table in this task.
acceptance_criteria: Project scope shows only tasks linked to that bb Project; All projects retains aggregate behavior and filtering; task creation always resolves a concrete Tasks project; missing or ambiguous links have an actionable empty or selection state; tests cover both scopes.

title: Add the claim and Continue locally user experience
description: Add employee-facing surfaces in personal bb for Jira-linked available work, reconnaissance choices, package details, claim confirmation, local materialization progress, offline readiness, and navigation to the created thread.
design: Build on the same SDK and CLI contracts rather than embedding lifecycle policy in the UI. Clearly distinguish central discovery state from local thread state and show repository, base revision, required access, package version, and last synchronization time.
acceptance_criteria: A user can select a continuation, understand what will be downloaded and executed, create or open the local thread, confirm it is ready for offline use, and recover from actionable authentication, Git, or compatibility failures.

title: Add native manager and child-session UI
description: Present conductor managers and child sessions through native bb navigation, status, timeline, and controls.
design: Group child sessions under the manager by parentThreadId. Add a manager header session cluster and run-level stop action; keep implementation-detail tasks in timeline rows rather than a second navigation tree.
acceptance_criteria: Users can understand run state from the manager, open any live child session, see backend and profile context, stop the run, and navigate the hierarchy on desktop and compact layouts.
